question.problem:
Given the orthogonal basis $B$ of ${R}^{2}$ and the vector $x$ below, find the value of $5{x}_{1},$ where ${x}_{1}$ is the first component of $[x]_{B}.$

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\},\,x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${q}_{1},\,{q}_{2}.$ 

Since $B$ is an orthogonal basis, we have that $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]$, where ${x}_{i}=\frac{x\cdot {q}_{i}}{{q}_{i}\cdot {q}_{i}}.$ Computing ${x}_{1},$ we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{x\cdot {q}_{1}}{{q}_{1}\cdot {q}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot (-4)+(-4)\cdot 2}{{(-4)}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-20-8}{20} \\  & =-\frac{7}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
5{x}_{1}=5\cdot (-\frac{7}{5})=-7.
$$
